title: Semantic Kernel Memory, Vector Stores & Embeddings
description: Implement short-term working memory, persistent vector search, and embedding generation using Semantic Kernel in .NET.

data.text: Enterprise AI applications need memory to maintain context. Semantic Kernel distinguishes between two complementary memory layers: Working Memory (short-term conversational state preserved inside ChatHistory across consecutive user turns) and Semantic Memory (long-term factual knowledge indexed into vector databases and recalled via high-dimensional embedding similarity).
In Semantic Kernel, text is translated into vector spaces using the ITextEmbeddingGenerationService. You can batch-generate embeddings for thousands of text passages efficiently.

data.text: Integrating Persistent Vector Stores with Semantic Kernel

Semantic Kernel aligns directly with Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData, allowing you to register vector connectors like Qdrant, Azure AI Search, or Redis, and expose semantic search directly as a plugin function to the kernel.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Semantic Kernel separates working conversational memory (ChatHistory) from long-term semantic memory (vector stores)
Use ITextEmbeddingGenerationService for fast, batch-oriented vector generation
Semantic Kernel v1.x integrates seamlessly with Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData connectors
Package vector retrieval into a [KernelFunction] plugin so agents can pull relevant context on demand
Always specify embedding dimensions and distance metrics matching the selected embedding model
data.takeaway: Memory gives AI workflows longevity. Combining ChatHistory for immediate conversation context with vector-backed semantic plugins enables agents to recall enterprise facts reliably.
